newsitem.title: UK: African cobalt output set to recover - Macquarie.
newsitem.headline: African cobalt output set to recover - Macquarie.

text.p: Cobalt production is expected to rise sharply over the next five years, mostly due to by-product production from a host of new nickel projects, but developments in Africa also point to a recovery in traditional players.
In its latest weekly review Macquarie Equities Ltd said perceptions that Zambia and Zaire are no longer major players could be off-beam.

"The general assumption among many cobalt market watchers is that the mining industry in that part of the world is now dead and that little recovery can be expected. This could be a seriously false assumption," Macquarie said.

In Zambia, production could rise to 4,500 tonnes as ZCCM has hit a high cobalt grade part of the Nchanga orebody. Production is projected to rise 6,000 tonnes in 1997 and then tail off towards 5,000 tonnes by 1998/99.
Also in Zambia, Colossal Resources has started recovering cobalt from a ZCCM tailing dump and hopes to raise production to 600 tonnes a year by 1997/98, Macquarie said.
Meanwhile in Zaire an improved political climate has generated a large interest in developing currently idled mining operations, as well as recovering cobalt and other materials from slag heaps.
The projects include possible joint ventures with Gecamines at Tenke Fungurume, Kambove, and Kakanda.
Also, America Mineral Fields has announced plans to re-open the idled Kipushi zinc/copper mine and is bidding with four other companies to recover cobalt and copper from tailings at Kilwezi.
All told, the various projects add up to as much as 20,000 tonnes of cobalt, compared with Zaire's likely 1996 level of 5,000 tonnes, it said. --London Newsroom, +44 171 542 8080
